tags.gist: Wants history completeness scored by recall of a case-locked required-question list written beforehand, never by the model grading itself.
Says re-asking a question already answered in the transcript should count as a reliability miss, not thoroughness.
Wants replay consistency required on action-relevant fields such as diagnosis family and next step, not on wording.
Wants guardrail tests scored pass or fail on visible output and required to hold across turns, since hard rules fail later.
Says hallucination checks cannot rely on regex over a fixed entity list; combine checks against sources with clinician review of samples.
Wants these measures re-run whenever the foundation-model identifier or the prompt template changes.
Prefers commonly defined test items alongside a hidden holdout set, with licensed clinicians reviewing only the decision gold.
Says the sketch under-weights multi-turn information gathering and run-to-run reliability, which prototype testing exposed and should be first-class elements.
Calls benchmarking plus risk-proportionate clinical confirmation the right frame.
Warns high knowledge or single-turn safety scores can mask conversational failures such as closing history early, repeating questions or inventing facts.
Says these product behaviors must be tested on the finished configuration of prompt, tools and served snapshot, and retested when it changes.
Reports models self-grading histories complete while omitting the decisive exposure question; asks for recall against a pre-specified question list for intake functions.
Says multi-turn risk includes failing to use state the device already collected, not only drift from information toward action.
Wants multi-turn intake benchmarked with an explicit already-answered set, scoring repeats of resolved questions as reliability misses.
Wants a repeated-run consistency metric on diagnosis family, site of care and test-or-treat decisions for fixed transcripts and pinned decoding.
Wants a small instruction-lock set of pinned negatives in nonclinical benchmarking, scored pass or fail and holding on later turns.
Says traceability to sources is part of risk assessment, since invented facts may surface in any clause and escape entity-list rules.
For documentation and history write-back, wants denial-aware source-conditioned checks plus clinician review of sampled sentences, not a clean regex report.
Summarizes seven asks: case-locked completeness scoring, repeat and consistency metrics, instruction-lock tests, open-ended hallucination checks, re-runs on change, hidden holdouts.
